features.name: visible_peak_mean_545_555
features.description: Mean intensity over the 545-555 nm visible crest; robust to single-band noise and captures overall signal height near the dominant peak.
features.expected_model_benefit: Gives trees a high-signal continuous split candidate for overall spectral magnitude in the main visible crest.

features.name: visible_peak_bucket
features.description: Ordinal bucket of the same visible crest using unsupervised cut points 600, 1000, 1500, and 2500 chosen from the training-fold intensity scale.
features.expected_model_benefit: Pre-binned intensity lets shallow trees isolate very dim, moderate, bright, and extreme spectra without learning several raw cut points.

features.name: blue_to_green_rise_norm
features.description: Normalized contrast between the blue shoulder around 451-465 nm and the visible crest around 545-555 nm.
features.expected_model_benefit: Highlights spectra whose visible crest rises sharply from the blue region, a nonlinear shape cue that trees can threshold directly.

features.name: green_to_red_drop_norm
features.description: Normalized contrast from the green-yellow crest to the red region near 651-663 nm.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures slope steepness after the main visible crest, giving trees an interaction-like shape feature rather than isolated bands.

features.name: orange_red_valley_depth_norm
features.description: Valley strength near 619-623 nm relative to neighboring shoulders at roughly 591 nm and 651 nm.
features.expected_model_benefit: Makes small absorption-like valley patterns easier for trees to use than comparing several neighboring raw bands independently.

features.name: red_edge_bump_norm
features.description: Local curvature around 693 nm versus adjacent readings near 681 nm and 701 nm.
features.expected_model_benefit: Second-derivative-like cue helps trees split on local bumps or dips around the red-edge transition.

features.name: near_red_tail_decay_norm
features.description: Normalized decrease from the early near-red region around 705-721 nm to the longer-wavelength low-signal tail around 751-800 nm.
features.expected_model_benefit: Summarizes tail collapse after about 700 nm as a single thresholdable feature for tree splits.

features.name: nir_low_signal_count
features.description: Count of selected long-wavelength bands with response below 1.0 intensity unit, indicating dropout or near-zero sensor response.
features.expected_model_benefit: Discrete count offers direct thresholds for low-signal and dropout patterns that may otherwise be spread across many bands.

features.name: narrow_spike_815_norm
features.description: Normalized narrow spike at 814.5 nm compared with immediate neighbors at 812.7 nm and 816.7 nm.
features.expected_model_benefit: Allows a tree split to isolate spectra with a detector-line spike or sharp local emission at this wavelength.

features.name: nir_bump_955_961_norm
features.description: Normalized bump around 955-961 nm relative to shoulders near 948 nm and 973 nm.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures broad long-wavelength bump or absorption contrast as a compact nonlinear feature for tree thresholds.

features.name: holistic_spectrum_shape_grade
features.description: Semantic row-level morphology grade: 0=flat or weak, 1=smooth single crest, 2=sharp crest with steep red decline, 3=multi-crest or strong long-wavelength texture, 4=irregular or noisy morphology. Use only the row spectrum and fixed training-fold scale references.
features.expected_model_benefit: Supplies coarse morphology grouping that trees can combine with precise numeric thresholds for robust splits.

features.name: acquisition_artifact_severity_grade
features.description: Semantic ordinal grade of acquisition artifacts: 0=clean, 1=mild narrow spikes, 2=several narrow spikes, 3=near-zero dropouts, 4=strong saturation or clipping, 5=severe mixed artifacts. Use only visible sensor patterns in the row and training-fold numeric ranges.
features.expected_model_benefit: Routes noisy or artifact-heavy rows into separate tree branches before finer spectral splits are applied.
